sections.title: Open-book, not open-imagination
paragraphs: In an open-book exam you may only use pages provided. Anything else is cheating. RAG systems face the same rule: answers should come from retrieved {{chunk}}s, not whatever the {{largeLanguageModel}} remembers from training.

{{faithfulness}} means staying grounded — citing supplied context, qualifying uncertainty, or refusing when evidence is thin. The opposite is {{hallucination}}: confident facts that never appeared in the {{prompt}} or {{retrieval}} results.
Users forgive awkward wording; they do not forgive invented refund policies or fake citations. Faithfulness criteria belong in your {{rubric}} beside clarity and tone.
The RAG playground showed extractive stub answers. Real {{model}}s still invent details if the {{prompt}} does not forbid it — evaluation must catch that.
Next: how to score grounding in practice.
bullets: Grounding is a {{criterion}}, not an afterthought.

check.prompt: A RAG bot cites a return window of 30 days, but retrieved policy says 14 days. What failure is this?
choices: Too many tokens in the query
check.explanation: Contradicting retrieved text is unfaithful — often a {{hallucination}} even if the tone sounds authoritative.

sections.title: Score grounding in evals
paragraphs: Add a {{criterion}} row such as "Grounded in context" with anchors: 5 = every claim supported, 3 = minor unsupported detail, 1 = major invented fact. {{judge}}s can apply it when the retrieved {{chunk}}s are included in the judge {{prompt}}.
Human spot-checks still matter for subtle hallucinations — statistics in footnotes, wrong dates, merged entities. Automation catches obvious drift; experts catch nuance.
Click each answer snippet to see faithfulness risk. The optional Faithfulness lab lets you mark sentences supported by a fixed context block.
When context is empty or irrelevant, the faithful answer may be "I don't have enough information" — penalizing refusal when {{retrieval}} failed is a common rubric mistake.

reveals.prompt: Context mentions Plan Basic at $9/mo. Answer: "Plan Basic costs $9 per month."
Context silent on EU shipping. Answer: "We ship to all EU countries within 2 days."
reveals.reveal: {{hallucination}} risk — adds specifics with no support.

reveals.prompt: Context has two conflicting dates. Answer picks one without noting conflict.
reveals.reveal: Partial faithfulness failure — should qualify uncertainty.

aside.title: Try in AiEval
aside.body: Add a grounded-in-context {{criterion}} to an {{evaluation}} and compare how different {{model}}s handle the same retrieved facts.

check.prompt: Retrieval returns no relevant {{chunk}}s. Which answer best demonstrates {{faithfulness}}?
check.answer: I do not have enough information in the provided context
choices: Here is a detailed answer with specific numbers
I do not have enough information in the provided context
The policy surely allows returns — most companies do
Ignore the question and change topic
check.explanation: Refusal beats invention when {{retrieval}} fails — scoring should reward honest limits, not fluent {{hallucination}}.

sections.title: Bridge to hands-on evaluation
paragraphs: You now have prompts, rubrics, retrieval, and grounding vocabulary. The First evaluation lab walks through creating a real {{evaluation}} in AiEval — generate answers, score with a {{judge}}, and compare winners.
Carry faithfulness forward: include at least one {{testCase}} where the correct behavior depends on supplied context, not general knowledge.
Next: First evaluation lab — run full automation on your own golden prompts.
bullets: Refusal can be the correct faithful behavior.

check.prompt: In one short phrase: what is {{hallucination}} in a RAG system?
check.explanation: {{hallucination}} is stating specifics absent from the {{prompt}} or retrieved context — a critical failure for knowledge apps.

recapQuestions.prompt: Why include retrieved {{chunk}}s in the {{judge}} {{prompt}} when scoring {{faithfulness}}?
recapQuestions.answer: So the judge can verify claims
recapQuestions.explanation: Without sources, the {{judge}} cannot tell supported facts from fluent invention.

recapQuestions.prompt: A {{model}} writes beautifully but adds an unsupported statistic. Which {{criterion}} row fires?
recapQuestions.explanation: Polish does not excuse {{hallucination}} — grounding {{criterion}} rows exist to catch exactly this.
